name: China-based Mustang Panda Observed Conducting Phishing Campaigns against European Entities
description:
In February 2022, Cisco Talos observed the China-based threat actor Mustang Panda conducting phishing campaigns against European entities, including Russian organizations. MustangPanda, also known as RedDelta or Bronze President, has targeted entities all over the world since at least 2012.

At the core
Some phishing messages contain malicious lures masquerading as official European Union reports on the conflict in Ukraine and its effects on NATO countries. Other phishing emails deliver fake "official" Ukrainian government reports, both of which download malware onto compromised machines.

name: Phishing Campaign by Chinese APT Group Mustang Panda Targets Russian Officials
description:
Researchers at Secureworks have discovered a phishing campaign that has been targeting Russian officials. The campaign has been linked to a Chinese APT group known as Mustang Panda.

The operation
Mustang Panda, also known as HoneyMyte and Bronze President, has previously been behind cyberespionage campaigns against European targets. The recently discovered campaign uses fake European Union (EU) documents containing sanction details against Belarus. Although the files appear as PDFs, they are EXE files that fetch malicious software like an encrypted PlugX variant, a malicious DLL loader, a digitally signed EXE file, etc. The DLL loader uses a legitimate signed file to perform DLL search order hijacking, which allows it to execute the PlugX malware payload.

description:

name: Chinese 'Mustang Panda' Hackers Spotted Deploying New 'Hodur' Malware
description:
A China-based advanced persistent threat (APT) known as Mustang Panda has been linked to an ongoing cyber espionage campaign using a previously undocumented variant of the PlugX remote access trojan on infected machines.

Slovak cybersecurity firm ESET dubbed the new version Hodur, owing to its resemblance to another PlugX (aka Korplug) variant called THOR that came to light in July 2021.

"Most victims are located in East and Southeast Asia, but a few are in Europe (Greece, Cyprus, Russia) and Africa (South Africa, South Sudan)," ESET malware researcher Alexandre Côté Cyr said in a report shared with The Hacker News.

name: Mustang Panda’s Hodur: Old tricks, new Korplug variant | WeLiveSecurity
description: ESET researchers have discovered a new variant of the Korplug malware used by an APT group known as Mustang Panda, which they attribute to a cyberespionage campaign targeting European diplomatic missions.

name: Mustang Panda Cyber Espionage Group Plants Malware Backdoor on Myanmar President’s Website
description: ESET research uncovered a supply chain attack on the Myanmar president office website (http://president-office.gov[.]mm). Attackers trojanized an archive containing fonts available for download on the homepage. The spearphishing campaigns mainly targeted Myanmar. They found a weak link with the APT group Mustang Panda (a timestamp in a .lnk file) but cannot confirm the attribution at this point.

name: CrimsonIAS Delphi Backdoor Possibly Linked to Mustang Panda
description: CrimsonIAS is a Delphi-written backdoor dating back to at least 2017 that enables operators to run command line tools, exfiltrate files, and upload files to the infected machine. CrimsonIAS is notable as it listens for incoming connections only; making it different from typical Windows backdoors that beacons out. The characteristics found in CrimsonIAS’s execution flow suggest a connection to Mustang Panda (aka BRONZE PRESIDENT, RedDelta) PlugX samples.  Based on those non-unique characteristics, ThreatConnect assesses with low confidence that CrimsonIAS is an additional tool in Mustang Panda’s repertoire.  Industry reporting assesses with varying levels of confidence that Mustang Panda is a Chinese espionage actor that has conducted operations in Mongolia, Vietnam, and Hong Kong among other locations.  According to fellow researchers, Mustang Panda targets non-government organizations (NGOs), law enforcement organizations, and political entities.

name: Mustang Panda (TA416) Using Golang PlugX Malware Loader
description: "Following the Chinese National Day holiday in September, Proofpoint researchers observed a resumption of activity by the APT actor TA416. Historic campaigns by this actor have also been publicly attributed to “Mustang Panda” and “RedDelta”. This new activity appears to be a continuation of previously reported campaigns that have targeted entities associated with diplomatic relations between the Vatican and the Chinese Communist Party, as well as entities in Myanmar. The targeting of organizations conducting diplomacy in Africa has also been observed. "
